title: Novel Splice Variants of Human TERT Suggest Deregulation of TERT RNA Splicing in Jurkat Cells and Other Cancer Cell Lines
content: Human TERT gene contains 16 exons, all of which are required to perform the major function of telomerase, namely telomere elongation of chromosomes following DNA replication. However, TERT protein is not dedicated solely to classical telomere elongation, whereas existence of numerous alternative TERT splice variants not possessing telomerase activity is considered as an important mechanism regulating both major and non-classical TERT functions. Thus, cataloging and classification of novel TERT splice variants presents a substantial interest for further understanding of TERT regulation and functions. In this study, we used PCR amplification of the hTERT RNA region located between exons 2 and 4, next generation sequencing as well as molecular cloning of amplified products to identify splice variants in the 5’ region of human TERT gene in Jurkat cells. In total, we identified 16 splice variants, 13 of which were not previously reported. The majority of non-classical splice events represents various combinations of four loci converted to pseudoexons in the large intron 2 of TERT gene. Importantly, two of these loci give rise to several overlapping pseudoexon variants differing in their exact border locations, which may suggest deregulation of splicing machinery and its incorrect function on TERT RNA. We also used nested PCR amplification and gel electrophoretic analysis to demonstrate that the range of splice variants between exons 2 and 4 is largely similar in Jurkat cells and six other cancer cell lines. Taken together, these results suggest the existence of splicing deregulation in the 5’ region of human TERT RNA in all cancer cell lines studied.
